setting.name: Show Disconnected Audio Devices
setting.casual_explanation: This makes disconnected audio devices appear in the classic Sound control panel. It is mainly useful for troubleshooting, advanced audio setup, or cleaning up stale devices.
setting.why_people_change_it: People enable it when they need to inspect endpoints that are currently unplugged or otherwise not active.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Showing disconnected devices can help debugging, but it can also expose stale or confusing entries that most users never need to see. This is a runtime-observed control-panel preference rather than a Microsoft-documented policy surface.
setting.professional_notes: The app writes ShowDisconnectedDevices = 1 under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Multimedia\Audio\DeviceCpl. On 2026-03-26, a Ghidra headless pass against mmsys.cpl decompiled the DeviceCpl flag handlers and showed SHGetValueW and SHSetValueW calls for ShowDisconnectedDevices and the same DeviceCpl branch. On 2026-03-27, the mapped v3.1 runtime runner re-ran the missing -> 1 -> missing cycle in Win25H2Clean, launched the classic Sound control panel, captured a WPR GeneralProfile placeholder trace, and preserved healthy shell state. That tightens the reversible-cycle and VM-safe-runner coverage, but the class-driving consumer proof still comes from the Procmon reads and the code-side proof still comes from the Ghidra pass. No primary Microsoft Learn or ADMX source for the DeviceCpl contract was captured in this pass, so the record remains a runtime-observed preference rather than a fully documented Microsoft contract.
